Chemistry and Biochemistry PhD
The PhD in Chemistry and Biochemistry at UMass Dartmouth provides both breadth and depth through a flexible structure of formal course work, independent study, and research. This full-time program takes approximately five years to complete. A minimum of 55 course credits is required beyond the BS, including at least 24 credits of formal courses (Including CHM 599 and CHM 699), at least 27 credits of doctoral dissertation research, and 4 credits of Graduate Seminar (CHM 650). A GPA of 3.0 or above on a 4.0 grading scale is required to satisfy the course requirements throughout the program. Doctoral students must also successfully pass written qualifying examinations, and the original research proposal-doctoral candidacy examination. The final part of the program is devoted principally to research leading to the doctoral dissertation. Doctoral students are required to successfully defend the dissertation research proposal and pass the dissertation defense, and complete a written dissertation.
Students entering the program with an earned master’s degree in chemistry or biochemistry may be eligible to receive Advanced Standing in the doctoral program. Such students complete a minimum of 8 credits from formal courses. The total number of formal course credits required will be determined during individual advisement with the Graduate Programs Director and must be approved by the Graduate Programs Committee. All other program requirements, including the qualifying examinations, remain unchanged.
Credit Requirements
Students must complete the following credit requirements as part of the program.
Core Courses (12 credits)
CHM 599 - Proseminar on Ethics Credits: 1
CHM 699 - Chemical Literature and Writing Credits: 2
Any three courses from the following five courses* in consultation with Research Advisor or the Graduate Programs Director:
CHM 510 - Advanced Organic Chemistry Credits: 3 or Organic substitution from list**
CHM 512 - Biochemistry II Credits: 3 or Biochemistry substitution from list**
CHM 541 - Principles of Inorganic Chemistry Credits: 3 or Inorganic substitution from list**
CHM 542 - Quantum Chemistry Credits: 3 or Physical substitution from list**
CHM 552 - Instrumental Methods of Analysis Credits: 4 or Analytical substitution from list**
**Allowed Equivalents in Each Division:
Organic Chemistry -
CHM 521 - Organic Mechanisms Credits: 3
Analytical Chemistry -
CHM 555 - Methods of Chemical Separation Credits: 3
Inorganic Chemistry -
Any inorganic 500-level courses except CHM 541
Biochemistry (choose from) -
CHM 511 - Biochemistry I Credits: 3
CHM 514 - Biochemistry Laboratory Credits: 3
CHM 529 - Physical Biochemistry Credits: 3
BMB 540 - Advanced Cell and Molecular Biology Credits: 3
Electives (12 credits)
Students must also complete 12 credits in elective coursework.
Any CHM 500+ level course chosen in consultation with Research Advisor
Dissertation (27 credits)
Candidates are required to complete a minimum of 27 credits in research.
CHM 600 - Thesis/Dissertation Research Credits: variable; .00 to 9.00
Seminar (4 credits)
Candidates must additionally complete 4 credits of graduate seminars.
CHM 650 - Graduate Seminar Credits: 1
